name: the dialog drops the source into the body as text again
why: A renderer that fell back to text would look almost right and be wrong on every heading, table and link.
grep: headings, emphasis, code spans and links become elements

name: underscore emphasis is 'restored'
why: Settings keys are snake_case; an underscore rule italicises the middle of sa_enable_caa_pics. The plausible 'improvement' is exactly this.
grep: a snake_case identifier is NOT italicised

name: any scheme is accepted as a link href
why: The text is fetched at runtime; a javascript: URL must render as inert text, never as a link.
grep: a non-http link renders as inert text

name: inline syntax is applied inside a fenced code block
why: A fence's content is content, not markup; the help file shows Markdown and settings strings in fences.
grep: fenced code keeps its content verbatim

name: the table separator row is not required
why: Without the separator guard a pipe-led prose line starts a table and the line after it vanishes into the skipped separator slot.
grep: a pipe-led line with no separator

name: a wrapped bullet ends its list (no lazy continuation)
why: Every fragment is individually well-formed, so reading the output does not show it; counting the lists does.
grep: a wrapped bullet stays ONE item

name: a lazy continuation need not be indented
why: Without the indent requirement a list swallows the heading under it.
grep: a heading directly under a list

name: <details> renders closed, as written
why: A quick filter that reports hits inside a closed box is worse than no filter.
grep: renders OPEN, so the quick filter

name: an in-document anchor is handed to the browser
why: The browser would scroll the page underneath the fixed dialog, and the table of contents would appear to do nothing.
grep: an in-document anchor link scrolls the dialog

name: heading ids lose their prefix, matching GitHub's bare slug
why: The prefix is what keeps a help heading's id from colliding with an id the host page already uses.
grep: an in-document anchor link scrolls the dialog

name: the Markdown stylesheet is never injected
why: Every class is still stamped, so the structure assertions pass; only a computed style sees the sheet missing.
grep: the stylesheet is actually injected

name: the fetched text is cached in GM storage
why: The whole point of the move: a GM value is handed to every page of the script, so a cached document is paid for on every page view.
grep: the text is kept in memory only

name: the copy in memory is not reused
why: Without it every open is a download; the in-memory copy is what replaces the old GM cache.
grep: the text is kept in memory only

name: Force refresh serves the copy in memory
why: The link would say Refreshed and show the old text.
grep: Force refresh fetches again

name: the quick filter hides non-matching blocks
why: Hiding paragraphs and headings out of prose destroys its reading order; the filter highlights only.

edits.replace: if (q) { _mdHighlight(body, q, markBg, markColor); body.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, p').forEach((el) => { if (!el.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(q)) el.style.display = 'none'; }); }

grep: non-matching content stays VISIBLE

name: clearing the highlights leaves split text nodes
why: The next query then misses matches that straddle the old mark boundaries.
grep: clearing the filter removes the highlights

name: Escape in the filter closes the whole dialog
why: The first Escape must only clear the query; losing the dialog there throws away the reader's place.

edits.replace:
// First Escape clears the field, the second leaves it; neither
                // closes the dialog.

grep: Escape clears the filter first

name: a click outside does not close it
why: The dialog would stay over the page until Escape or the ✕.
grep: a click outside closes it

name: the geometry is not stored on close
why: geometryKey would be accepted and silently do nothing.
grep: with geometryKey the position and size are stored

name: Retry does not fetch again
why: After a failure the dialog could never recover without being closed and reopened.
grep: a failed fetch shows the error with Retry
